task.description: Fix GH #500 (ISS-0172, MAJOR): src/lua_test_root.zig's type-only pin pattern (`_ = lua.instruction_limiter.InstructionLimiter;`) does not force struct field-type resolution or function-body analysis, so zig build test-lua reports green while src/lua/instruction_limiter.zig:39 (a discarded c_int return value from lua_sethook) and src/lua/memory_limiter.zig:13 (std.Thread.Mutex, which does not exist in Zig 0.16) both contain hard compile errors that are never surfaced. This affects 8 test roots using the same pattern: src/lua_test_root.zig, src/simulation_test_root.zig, src/transition_test_root.zig, src/oidc_test_root.zig, src/oidc_jit_test_root.zig, src/config_idp_test_root.zig, src/core_modules_test_root.zig, src/repository_test_root.zig. This is a two-part fix: (1) FIX THE 2 REAL BUGS this gap hid -- instruction_limiter.zig's discarded c_int return (use `_ = bindings.lua_sethook(...)` or handle the return value properly per whatever the correct behavior is) and memory_limiter.zig's nonexistent std.Thread.Mutex field (Zig 0.16's actual Mutex type -- check std.Thread's current API, it likely moved or was renamed); (2) FIX THE PIN PATTERN across all 8 test roots to a form that forces both struct field-type resolution (e.g. `_ = @sizeOf(T);` or `_ = @typeInfo(T).@"struct".fields;`) and function-body analysis (a real, non-comptime-eliminated call or @TypeOf-based reference), per the issue's own acceptance criteria. Verify by DELIBERATE MUTATION for BOTH failure shapes (a bad field type in a struct, and a statement error in an unreferenced function) -- the target must go red in both cases, and you must actually perform this mutation test, not just reason about it. Also correct src/lua_test_root.zig's header comment, which currently overclaims what its prior mutation-verification covered. This is a real, well-specified fix with concrete mechanical steps across 8 files plus 2 genuine bug fixes -- work through it methodically, file-by-file. If the pin-pattern fix and the tools/lint_test_wiring.py enhancement (flagging type-only pins) require a non-trivial design decision about exactly which @typeInfo/@sizeOf incantation generalizes cleanly across all 8 files' different type shapes, route to CODE-DESIGNER; if it's mechanical enough to do directly, you may implement yourself and route straight to TEST-RUNNER -- use your judgment, explain either way.
acceptance_criteria: instruction_limiter.zig c_int discard fixed with correct handling
memory_limiter.zig std.Thread.Mutex fixed to whatever Zig 0.16 actually provides
Pin pattern fixed across all 8 named test roots to force both struct field-type resolution and function-body analysis
Deliberate mutation test ACTUALLY PERFORMED for both failure shapes (bad field type, statement error in unreferenced function) -- target confirmed to go red in both cases
tools/lint_test_wiring.py enhanced to flag a test root whose pins are type-only
src/lua_test_root.zig header comment corrected to accurately state what mutation shapes were tested
zig build exits 0 after all fixes (the 2 real bugs are now fixed, not just detected)

result.summary: Fixed both real bugs GH #500/ISS-0172 called out (src/lua/instruction_limiter.zig:39's discarded lua_sethook c_int return -- confirmed already correctly fixed to `_ = bindings.lua_sethook(...)` on this branch's base; src/lua/memory_limiter.zig's nonexistent std.Thread.Mutex -- confirmed already replaced with atomic counters on this branch's base). Both were already fixed on main by prior ISS-0169/ISS-0174 work before this run started; verified by reading current source and git log. Found and fixed a THIRD, previously-undiscovered real bug of the same class while strengthening the pin pattern: src/lua/structured_logger.zig's StructuredLogger.log() called std.io.getStdErr(), which does not exist in Zig 0.16 -- invisible because the method was only ever bare-pinned (`_ = lua.structured_logger.StructuredLogger;`), never called or refAllDecls'd directly. Fixed to std.debug.print, matching this codebase's established Zig-0.16 stderr idiom. Fixed the pin pattern across all 8 named test roots (src/lua_test_root.zig plus 7 others: simulation, transition, oidc, oidc_jit, config_idp, core_modules, repository). Root cause has THREE distinct blind spots, all confirmed by empirical probe against this Zig 0.16 installation: (1) a bare `_ = Module.Type;` reference resolves the type NAME but not its struct/union/enum FIELD types (Zig resolves those lazily); (2) refAllDecls(module) does not descend into an imported submodule's function bodies at all when called through a mod.zig-style aggregator (affects simulation_test_root.zig, repository_test_root.zig, which both aggregate via mod.zig); (3) refAllDecls does not descend into a struct's own METHOD bodies even when called directly on the type's enclosing single-file module, because a method is a declaration of the struct, not of the module (affects all 8 roots for any struct with methods). Fix: (a) refAllDecls called directly on every LEAF file, never only on a mod.zig aggregator; (b) a shared `pinModuleTypes(T)` helper duplicated per-file (consistent with each shim's existing self-contained-shim style) that does `_ = @sizeOf(field)` (closes gap 1) plus `refAllDecls(field)` called directly on each struct/union/enum type (closes gaps 2 and 3 together, since it forces both field-type resolution and analysis of the type's own methods). instruction_limiter.zig, memory_limiter.zig and timeout.zig's TimeoutContext keep their existing real-call coverage in lua_test_root.zig (strictly stronger than either pin). MANDATORY MUTATION TESTING PERFORMED FOR REAL (not just reasoned about), both failure shapes, on BOTH src/lua_test_root.zig (the file the issue specifically calls out) AND src/simulation_test_root.zig (the mod.zig-aggregator shape, spot-checked as the second-most-structurally-different root): (1) bad field type (std.Thread.NonExistentMutex injected into MemoryLimiter / ServiceCatalog / PlatformClock) -- confirmed target goes red in all cases, then reverted; (2) statement type-error in an unreferenced struct METHOD body (ServiceCatalog.lookup / PlatformUuidSource method / isActive()) -- confirmed target goes red in all cases (trace shows pinModuleTypes -> refAllDecls catching it), then reverted. All 7 other test roots rebuilt individually after applying the fix; zero previously-hidden errors surfaced in 6 of them (repository, oidc, oidc_jit, config_idp, core_modules, transition -- all pass same test counts as before). simulation_test_root.zig also surfaced none once mutation-reverted. Only lua_test_root.zig's OWN strengthened pins (for StructuredLogger/ServiceCatalog/Event/TimeSource, previously bare-pinned) surfaced the third real bug (structured_logger.zig), which was fixed as required by the Unblock-Everything directive. Corrected src/lua_test_root.zig's header comment ('What is actually verified here' section), which previously overclaimed mutation coverage (its cited mutation targeted a function body already reached via a register() decl, not the two ISS-0172 blind spots) -- now accurately documents both confirmed blind spots, the real mutation evidence for each, and which types get real-call coverage vs pinModuleTypes coverage. Enhanced tools/lint_test_wiring.py with an ADVISORY-only (non-blocking) check, find_type_only_pins(), that flags src/*_test_root.zig bare `_ = a.b.CapitalizedType;` pins with no @sizeOf/refAllDecls coverage for that type elsewhere in the file; validated it correctly flags the exact original ISS-0172 bug pattern (InstructionLimiter/MemoryLimiter) when run against the pre-fix git history version of lua_test_root.zig. It remains advisory (exit 0) because a regex/line-scan cannot prove a bare-pinned type has no real coverage through a call elsewhere -- consistent with every other tools/lint_*.py in this repo being line-scan-based, not semantic. Design decision: implemented directly rather than routing to CODE-DESIGNER -- despite real per-file variance in exactly which types/methods each of the 8 roots has, the generalizing fix (pinModuleTypes helper + direct-leaf refAllDecls) is mechanical and uniform once derived, and deriving it required empirical probing of Zig 0.16 semantics (which I did directly) rather than a product/architecture decision -- there was no genuine design ambiguity, only an investigation. Validation: zig build exits 0; zig build test-env-verify exits 0 HEALTHY 10/10 checks (after unsetting a stale shell-inherited BPM_TEST_DB_URL pointing at a sibling workspace's port -- pure environment artifact, not a code or infra defect, resolved as part of Unblock-Everything); zig build test exits 0, 87/87 steps succeeded, 965/1029 tests passed (64 skipped) -- identical pass/skip counts confirmed via git stash before/after, zero regressions from the pin-pattern change.
